construction: 16 parts in 3 steps. Step 1: a 12-stud wall of three 4863 1×4×2 windows with six 4862 glass panes. Step 2: a 1×8 and a 1×6 plate (and a 1×1 plate) capping the wall. Step 3: four 4857 4×4 double-slope hinge bricks forming the roof.
interfaces: Stud directions: 16 parts, all up. The window wall's underside meets the fuselage floor plates; the hinge fingers on the far edge of the roof bricks meet the hinge on the parent's other wall.
lesson: The openable roof of the classic City airliner: four 4×4 double-slope bricks with a hinge edge sit on one wall of window bricks; the opposite wall in the parent carries the matching hinge, so the whole roof lifts to load minifigures.
parent_context: `6392 - airplane.ldr` places it at (200, −156, −35) with matrix −1 0 0 / 0 1 0 / 0 0 −1, a 180° turn about Y: the section becomes the right-hand cabin wall and roof. The same design appears in 10159.
reuse_notes: Use it when a cabin must open without removing the roof: one wall carries the roof bricks, the other the hinge, and the cabin width is fixed by the 4×4 double slopes (four studs across). Window bricks give the row of cabin windows for free.
